Validation / Acceptance Criteria: 1) Default value comparison for each readable register equals its documented reset value → Pass. 2) Readback after masked write matches the expected value derived from the write mask, read mask, and default value → Pass. 3) No default-value or write/read mismatches at test end → Pass.
Hidden_Test_Description: Performs two checks on PCIe0 SII RC registers: (1) Default reset value verification by iterating addr_array and, for each entry that is readable (read_mask_array[i] != 0x00000000) and not the PHY reset control register, reading the register value and comparing it against default_value_array[i]. (2) Write/read verification by writing a sequence of test patterns to each address that is not marked in skip_array and that is writable (write_mask_array[i] != 0x00000000), then reading back all addresses that are both writable and readable and comparing the read value to an expected value computed with masks and defaults. The test accumulates failures in def_fail_cnt and wr_fail_cnt and finishes with failure if any mismatch occurs; otherwise it finishes with success.
Hidden_Remarks: Addresses with read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 are skipped for reading. Addresses with write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 are skipped for writing and verification. Entries with skip_array[i] == 1 are skipped for both write and read phases. The entry equal to mizar_PCIE0_SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL is excluded from default value verification. The optional soft reset sequence is present but commented out and not executed.
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: Initialization: def_fail_cnt=0; wr_fail_cnt=0. Default value check (chk_rst_val): For i from 0 to CNT-1: addr=addr_array[i]; if (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; if (addr_array[i] == mizar_PCIE0_SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL) continue; data_rd = read_reg(addr); if (data_rd == default_value_array[i]) pass; else { def_fail_cnt++; log failure with Addr, Expected, Read_data }. Write/read check (chk_rd_wr): Define chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each j in 0..5: data_wr = chk_val[j]; Write phase: For i from 0 to CNT-1: addr=addr_array[i]; if (skip_array[i] == 1) continue; if (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; else write_reg(addr, data_wr). Read/verify phase: For i from 0 to CNT-1: addr=addr_array[i]; if (skip_array[i] == 1) continue; if (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; if (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; else { data_rd = read_reg(addr); wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff); exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])); if (data_rd == exp_val) pass; else { wr_fail_cnt++; log mismatch with Address, Expected value, Read value } }. Test completion (test_case): Call chk_rst_val(); Call chk_rd_wr(); If (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1); else finish(0).

Remarks: Execution depends on compile-time defines for role and instance. Coherency control is programmed before configuration space transactions. Readiness is gated by status polling and a scratch register handshake.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Program DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF on both instances to set coherency-related fields.
2) Poll status registers until the link and readiness conditions are satisfied.
3) Initialize the scratch/handshake register and wait for system stabilization.
4) Read configuration space fields for identification and baseline values.
5) Write and then read back the BAR registers to observe reported masks and sizes.
6) Program BAR registers with specific base values and read back to confirm configuration.
7) Enable memory space, I/O space, and bus mastering via the command register.
8) Poll the scratch/handshake register until the expected completion value is observed and then conclude the test.
